teaser.text: Freeport-McMoRan is a mining and metals company whose main product is copper, sold in several forms. To understand its business, follow a dollar from rock through processing, sale and the costs that remain.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Freeport-McMoRan, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The bear case falls from $5.755 billion to $4.88 billion as weak prices and an interrupted restart leave capacity underused. The bull case reaches $17.76 billion before easing to $17.99 billion in 2029, reflecting strong prices, timely gold and repeatable leach output. FCX’s 2025 copper sales and Grasberg production both fell sharply, while the latest quarter still showed $7,029 million of revenue and $2,003 million of operating income.

The base case reaches $76.20 first and $87.00 last. Its 55% probability is highest because it follows management’s staged recovery without assuming every growth project succeeds. High capex and partner distributions prevent a faster improvement in cash and valuation.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Freeport-McMoRan really make?

paragraphs.text: In 2025, operations generated $5.610 billion, while capital spending consumed $4.494 billion. The stated remainder was $1.079 billion; after stock-based compensation, Freeport’s analytical “real free cash flow” was $958 million. Its margin was 3.7%, far below the 24.0% achieved in 2021.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Freeport-McMoRan today?

paragraphs.text: The trailing P/E is 34.4x, based on completed earnings. The forward P/E is 16.4x, based on a forecast. Those multiples imply earnings per share rising from about US$2.03 to US$4.26. The lower multiple is therefore not a second price: it is the same price applied to a much more optimistic earnings assumption.

blocks.heading: How much does Freeport-McMoRan pay per share?

paragraphs.text: The base dividend stays at $0.60 per share in every window. The bear case cuts it to $0.30 after 2027, while the bull case raises it to $0.80 and then $1.00. The base reflects four consecutive years at $0.60 and current 2026 guidance. The downside reflects distributions that exceeded free cash flow in several recent years; the upside requires stronger cash after capital spending and partner distributions.

blocks.heading: Does Freeport-McMoRan's cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: The operating picture is lower production at 2,376 million pounds alongside a higher realized copper price of $4.75 per pound. Net debt reached $5,555 million in 2025. The company’s real free cash flow was $0.66 per share, while distributions to minority owners, dividends, and buybacks exceeded it by $0.81 per share. At $69.87, the stock’s free cash flow yield is 1.1%. Its dividend yield is 0.9%.

In 2025, operations generated $5.610 billion, while capital spending consumed $4.494 billion. The stated remainder was $1.079 billion; after stock-based compensation, Freeport’s analytical “real free cash flow” was $958 million. Its margin was 3.7%, far below the 24.0% achieved in 2021.

earnings.title: Freeport-McMoRan earnings date
earnings.meta_description: Freeport-McMoRan's October 27, 2026 results will test sales, deferred Indonesian gold and the Grasberg recovery.
earnings.opening: Freeport-McMoRan's next results are expected on October 27, 2026. Watch whether Freeport-McMoRan converts its recovery schedule into safe, repeatable shipments and cash.
earnings.closing: The full Freeport-McMoRan research also covers its business, rivals, management and risks.

paragraphs.text: For 2026, Freeport projects sales of 3,057 million pounds of copper, 654 thousand ounces of gold and 93 million pounds of molybdenum. Sales are not the same as production. At PT Freeport Indonesia, or PTFI, copper concentrate must pass through smelting and refining before the finished metal can be sold.

The annual unit net cash-cost target is $1.90 per pound. That measure excludes idle-facility and restoration costs, which are expected to total about $1.2 billion in 2026. So falling unit costs would show better operating leverage, but not the full economic cost of restarting Grasberg.

blocks.heading: Has Freeport-McMoRan kept its recent promises?

paragraphs.text: For 2025, the annual formula produced 99.6% of target. After work-related fatalities and the Grasberg mud rush, the compensation committee reduced Quirk’s and Adkerson’s awards to 66.7% of target. The longer-term 2023–2025 awards still paid 125% because they measured a different period and different results.

Freeport also reported completing Bagdad’s autonomous-haulage conversion and restoring Indonesian smelter operations after the October 2024 fire. Those are real deliveries, though completion alone does not prove good returns or safe operations.

blocks.heading: What is Freeport-McMoRan's eight-quarter revenue and profit trend?

paragraphs.text: The eight-quarter pattern shows an uneven rebound. Revenue and margins recovered from the December trough, but the March insurance gain and June insurance receipt belong to different accounting periods. Comparing those quarters without separating the timing would mistake settlement accounting for operating improvement.
